newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Retail investors pile into Intel.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Retail investors pile into Intel.

text.p: Interest in Intel Corp options surged Thursday as the stock continued to rally into record territory after the company's bullish comments late Wednesday.
Traders said most of the activity was from retail investors after heavy institutional buying Wednesday.
By 1020 CST (1620 GMT), Intel shares were up 3-1/8 at 122, after reaching an all-time intraday high of 122-1/2 in early trading.
Turnover remained heavy as about 6.5 million shares changed hands by 1020 CST (1620 GMT).
After the close of trading Wednesday, the chip maker said it expected fourth quarter revenues and gross margins to beat the third quarter's $5.14 billion and 57 percent, respectively.
Heavy options activity Wednesday, particularly in the November 115 calls, was mainly speculative buying by institutions, traders said.
Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners in New York, said retail investors were jumping on the Intel options bandwagon Thursday.
"Today the follow-through is almost entirely retail," he said. "There's just enormous retail buying. All the retail firms are out there buying by the hundreds."
Most action was on the call side, led by the November 120, which traded about 5,950 contracts by 1030 CST (1630 GMT).
It gained 1-3/8 to four. Its open interest, boosted by the addition of 1,208 contracts Wednesday, was 8,171 contracts.
The December 120 call traded more than 5,200 contracts. It rallied 2-1/8 to 7-3/4. Open interest was 4,652.
"There's just huge customer demand for calls," Schwarz said.
Other busy Intel calls included the November 115, which traded about 3,550 contracts, the November 125, which traded nearly 3,400 and the December 125, which traded 2,230.
The most active put was the November 115. The option, which fell 50 percent to 3/4, traded about 2,350 contracts. Its open interest was 2,510 and included about 1,815 added Wednesday.

Schwarz noted that volatilities on the Intel calls rose moderately Wednesday but increased more substantially amid the heavy retail buying Thursday. -Gregory Crawford, 312-408-8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com
